In addition, by integrating an elliptic curve-based certificateless encryption mechanism, our scheme minimizes computational overhead and enhances overall efficiency. Further, the performance analysis proves that the proposed scheme has higher computational efficiency than other existing schemes.

articleTitle: An Attribute Similarity-Based Approach to Compress and Merge Alarms of Multiple Microservice Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: In microservice architecture, due to the fine-grained service splitting, a large number of alarm messages will be generated, which, if not processed, will lead to the operation and maintenance personnel drowning in the sea of alarms, thus missing the real critical problems. Therefore, this paper proposes an attribute similarity-based alarm compression and merging method for multiple micro service applications, which aims to reduce redundant alarms and improve the accuracy and processing efficiency of alarms. In this study, the seasonal and trend characteristics of monitoring indicators are eliminated by the time-series decomposition algorithm STL, and the multivariate time-series prediction of the residual series of multiple indicators is performed based on the vector autoregressive model VAR, and whether the microservices are abnormal is judged based on the Euclidean distances of the vectors; according to the characteristics of the ASON alarms of an actual electric power communication network, the communication alarm correlation model based on the hierarchical attribute similarity is established. Finally, a compression and merging method of multiple microservice application alarms based on attribute similarity is used in a real power system communication network. The test results show that by merging similar alarms, the number of alarms is reduced, which helps the operation and maintenance personnel to filter out the real problems that need attention from a large number of alarm messages. Moreover, the alarm compression and merging method based on attribute similarity has significant technical advantages in improving operation and maintenance efficiency, optimizing alarm management, and reducing operation and maintenance costs.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimal Communication Mode Selection Based on Pareto Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: This paper addresses the inefficiencies in human-composed communication mode forms and the unreasonable allocation of communication resources in the Foshan Power Grid. It requires software automation to generate forms, incorporating automatic mode type recognition, cross-system resource queries, routing analysis, and resource allocation modules to effectively improve the automation of communication business access. Routing analysis is the most crucial part of the form generation. This paper proposes an optimal communication routing selection algorithm based on Pareto optimization. By deeply exploring the principles of Pareto optimization, especially in routing analysis, multi-objective optimization is used to balance several key indicators (efficiency, safety, redundancy) in communication mode selection. Experiments show that the Pareto optimization-based automatic form generator provides routing results close to those manually selected, solving key challenges in the further design of automated communication mode robots.

articleTitle: The Lightweight Steel Surface Defect Detection Algorithm Based on YOLO-ETG
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: To address the current challenges of complex structures, inadequate detection accuracy, and excessive para meters in steel surface defect detection models, this paper pr oposes a lightweight detection algorithm, YOLO-ETG (YOLOv8-EfficientNet, Triplet attention and ghostconv). The algor ithm utilizes EfficientNet in the feature extraction stage to r educe model parameters and introduces a low-parameter Tri plet-attention mechanism in the feature fusion phase to enha nce the capture of semantic information related to defect fea tures. Additionally, Ghostconv is employed for convolution o ptimization, further reducing parameters and computational load. In the prediction phase, the loss function is optimized t o WIOU to improve the model's convergence efficiency and speed. Experimental results show that YOLO-ETG outperfor ms YOLOv8n on the NEU-DET dataset, with a 300% reducti on in model parameters and a 69% reduction in floating-poi nt operations, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 78.1% and a 1% improvement in detection accuracy. This d emonstrates that YOLO-ETG effectively enhances the precisi on of steel defect detection while maintaining lightweight cha racteristics, meeting practical production needs.

articleTitle: Improved White Shark Algorithm Based on Chaotic Mapping and Quadratic Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: To solve the problem of easily falling into local optima and low convergence accuracy of optimization results in white shark and optimization algorithms, an improved white shark optimization algorithm is proposed. In the population initialization phase, the sine chaotic mapping is used to initialize the population, enhancing the diversity of the population and improving the algorithm's search capability across the entire solution space; in the position update phase, a quadratic interpolation strategy is introduced to enhance the algorithm's local exploitation capability. Performance comparison experiments are conducted on 10 benchmark test functions, and the results show that the SWSO outperforms its comparative algorithms, with faster convergence speed and higher solution accuracy.

articleTitle: Distributed Data Sharing and Access Control in Industrial IoT Using Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), secure and efficient data sharing has become crucial for enabling industrial automation and smart transformation. However, existing centralized solutions face limitations in scalability, latency, and data privacy. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a blockchain-based distributed data-sharing and access control system tailored for resource-constrained industrial edge networks. The system adopts a three-layer architecture that integrates edge computing and blockchain technology to provide decentralized, low-latency data management. A novel smart contract framework is introduced to enforce multi-level access control and support fine-grained permissions for intra-domain and cross-domain data sharing. Experimental results show the system's improved performance in data access efficiency and throughput, offering a robust solution for real-time, secure IIoT applications.

articleTitle: Study on Computer Network Routing Optimization Algorithm Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: Traditional routing protocols, such as RIP and OSPF, encounter a series of issues—including slow convergence and high average latency—when faced with the exponential growth of network traffic and varying service demands. To address these challenges, routing algorithms leverage the powerful capabilities of deep reinforcement learning, enabling autonomous learning and optimization of network routing, thereby better adapting to complex network environments and fluctuating traffic demands. For the optimization of continuous state spaces, a routing optimization algorithm named DDPGOR (Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient On Routing) has been designed based on the aforementioned control mechanism. This algorithm employs Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks as recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and incorporates an attention mechanism to capture the relationships among various network traffic streams. In addition, to enhance the correlation among network traffic, we optimized the LSTM network by utilizing bidirectional LSTM networks instead of standard LSTM networks. Bidirectional LSTMs can capture longer-term information and identify correlations in network traffic from both forward and backward directions. Simulation results indicate that both DDPGOR and TD3OR significantly improve convergence and stability, markedly reduce end-to-end latency, and enhance throughput and link utilization compared to traditional routing algorithms. Furthermore, as an optimized version of the DDPGOR algorithm, the TD3OR algorithm outperforms DDPGOR in all performance metrics.

Author Keywords: Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory Network

articleTitle: Design and Image Enhancement Research of an Embedded Finger Vein Imaging Acquisition System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: Finger vein recognition technology has attracted widespread attention in the field of biometrics due to its high security and reliability in recent years. The key of finger vein recognition is the acquisition of finger vein image. Focusing on this issue, an embedded finger vein imaging acquisition system is designed for convenient identification, which is of good cost-performance ratio and strong real-time capability. The system uses the STM32F407ZGT6 as the main control chip and captures the infrared light illuminated by the finger vein through the OV2640 module for imaging. The collected finger vein images are then transmitted to the PC in real-time via USB communication. However, considering the uneven absorption of near-infrared light by the finger joint structure, which leads to issues such as uneven illumination, low contrast, and blurred edge details in the images, this study conducted research on image enhancement, such as image preprocessing and edge extraction, to facilitate the establishment of subsequent high-quality recognition model.

articleTitle: Capacity Prediction and Modeling of Virtual Energy Storage System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: To optimize the dispatch of Electric Vehicle Virtual Energy Storage (EVVES) across wide-ranging networks, this research presents a highly precise virtual energy storage capacity estimation model. By clustering the types of EVs participating in EVVES service, and taking into account the usage habits of various EV owners (e.g. daily mileage, charging/discharging pattern, expected spare travel power, etc.), the influence of the market on the responsiveness of EVVES, and the design of the available energy storage capacity redundancy, etc., we will comprehensively establish a virtual energy storage capacity estimation model for scheduling. Seamlessly aligned with the requirements of the power system, the model formulates tailored EVVES supply-demand matching strategies for various remunerated auxiliary services, including emergency power augmentation, peak-valley balancing, and seamless integration of renewable energy outputs. Employing Monte Carlo simulation, the model demonstrates exceptional accuracy in real-time estimation of the available capacity for VES services across distinct timeframes, thereby establishing a robust framework for the successful operationalization and subsequent scaling of EVVES initiatives. This work lays a cornerstone for advancing the practical application of EVVES in contemporary energy systems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Tracking Intelligent Car Design
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: The magnetic intelligent car following system is an automatic control technology based on electromagnetic induction principle, used to enable the car to autonomously navigate and run along a predetermined path or magnetic tape track. The system detects changes in the magnetic field on the ground through the electromagnetic sensors installed on the bottom of the car, thereby judging the position and direction of the car. Based on the feedback signal from the sensor, the microcontroller of the car will issue corresponding control instructions, driving the motor to adjust the speed and steering angle of the wheels, so that the car can run along the predetermined track steadily.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cross-Modal Retrieval with Low-Rank Multi-Head Self-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: In today's rapidly developing technological innovation environment, cross-modal retrieval plays a vital role in the field of modern information retrieval and data analysis. It can map data of different modalities such as images and text into a common semantic space, thereby realizing cross-modal similarity measurement and retrieval. In the field of patent analysis, image-text cross-modal retrieval is particularly important. Patent documents usually contain complex technical descriptions and related instructions. The ability to efficiently and accurately retrieve images and text from massive patent data is of great significance for technological innovation, competition analysis and intellectual property protection. This paper proposes a novel visual semantic embedding model for patents using a low-rank multi-head self-attention mechanism to improve the cross-modal retrieval performance in the field of patent analysis. Our model uses EfficientNet as an image encoder to extract richer and more detailed feature representations from patent images. The text encoder uses BERT to effectively handle the complex text structure and polysemy problems in patent documents. By optimizing the embedding generation process of the image-text encoder, the feature expression ability and retrieval accuracy of the model are significantly enhanced. At the same time, we introduced a multi-instance embedding network and used a new low-rank multi-head self-attention mechanism to combine global features and local features, and calculated multiple different representations of instances, further improving the model's ability to handle ambiguity and data diversity. To verify the effectiveness of the model, we conducted a large number of experiments on multiple public cross-modal datasets and a patent-specific dataset. The experimental results show that the model significantly outperforms most existing methods in multiple indicators, especially in patent image and text retrieval tasks, showing higher accuracy and robustness, providing a strong tool support for future patent analysis and technological innovation.

articleTitle: Imbalanced Phosphorylation Site Prediction Based on Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: With the development of biotechnology, the number and variety of proteins in databases are increasing rapidly. Post-translational modification (PTM) is a major way to regulate protein function and finding protein phosphorylation sites from a large number of protein sequences is crucial for disease research and drug development. Recently, many scholars have been devoted to developing computational predictors based on deep learning architectures for phosphorylation site prediction, but these methods are usually trained on independent databases. This paper explores a new method, PhosFLID, which uses federated learning to improve the accuracy of protein phosphorylation site prediction models and evaluates the effectiveness of this method on different imbalanced dataset. PhosFLID outperforms current leading methods and can be extended to multiple databases while ensuring the privacy of medical data. The research results show that the protein phosphorylation site prediction model using federated learning demonstrates better performance, improving prediction accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: LLMNDC: A Novel Approach for Network Device Configuration based on Fine-tuned Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: As networking demands continue to expand, there is an increasing need for enhanced capabilities in network device configuration. Managing network device configurations has become increasingly critical due to the expansion of network scales and complexity. Correct configurations ensure network security, performance, and reliability, yet traditional methods struggle with numerous parameters and complex dependencies. This complexity is exacerbated by varied configuration syntax and structures across different devices, further complicating management. To address these challenges, we propose a novel approach utilizing specially fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) to assist in automating network device configuration. This study integrates artificial intelligence and machine learning to provide configuration recommendations, enhancing the automation level in network device management. Our experiments demonstrate the model's capability in querying general data communication knowledge and providing specific configuration suggestions tailored to manufacturers such as Huawei and Cisco. These results enhance the automation and intelligence of network device configuration processes, providing crucial data support and introducing new technical approaches to the field.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Method Based on Siamese Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: Bearing components are important parts of mechanical equipment and have a significant impact on the operating status of the equipment. However, in actual industrial production, the data generated by bearing components is characterized by high dimensionality, nonlinearity, insufficient fault data, noise content, and operating load variation. Traditional machine learning methods for fault detection require human selection of fault features, and their reliability cannot be guaranteed. Therefore, to address the above problems, this paper proposes a fault detection model based on Siamese Convolutional Neural Networks (Siamese CNN) and conducts experiments on the benchmark bearing fault dataset collected by the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) data center. The results show that the average detection accuracy of the model reaches 99.6% under four working conditions, which is 0.4% higher than that of the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) model; the detection accuracy of the model is still higher than that of the CNN model in the case of fewer training samples and stronger noise; the average detection accuracy of the Siamese CNN model reaches 98.87%, which is 3.98% higher than that of the CNN model under six variable load cases and the detection accuracy of the model reaches 97% for all of the six variable load The detection accuracy of the Siamese CNN model reaches 98.87% on average, which is 3.98 % higher than that of the CNN model, and the detection accuracy in the six variable load cases reaches over 97%. The experiment fully verifies the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Robust Semi-Supervised Community Detection Based on Symmetric Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: The symmetric nonnegative matrix factorization (SNMF) model, renowned for its interpretability and efficiency, has been extensively adopted for community detection in the domain of complex networks. However, existing SNMF-based approaches exhibit limitations, particularly in capitalizing on limited supervisory information for enhanced detection performance and in their vulnerability to data distortion due to non-Gaussian noise and outliers. To overcome these limitations, a novel SNMF-based community detection method, namely correntropy-based semi-supervised SNMF (CSSNMF), is proposed in this paper for boosting the performance of SNMF-based methods in community detection tasks. More specifically, CSSNMF is characterized by two principal innovations: 1) adopting the pairwise constraints propagation (PCP) algorithm to fully utilize a small amount of supervisory information for reconstructing a more informative adjacency matrix; 2) using the correntropy instead of the traditional squared Frobenius norm as the similarity measure in SNMF for enhancing the robustness against noise and outliers. Notably, the learned adjacency matrix is not only utilized as the decomposed matrix within the SNMF model, but also integrated into the graph regularization for deriving a discriminative community indicator matrix. Moreover, the proposed method is delved into a thorough analysis for computational complexity. Through extensive experimental evaluations, the superiority of CSSNMF in terms of effectiveness and robustness has been demonstrated in community detection applications, particularly when bench marked against several leading SNMF-based methods on real-world networks with and without significant noise interference.

articleTitle: MFPD-Net: Multiscale Feature Fusion-based Photovoltaic Panel Defect Detection Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: With the rapid development of photovoltaic technology, ensuring the quality of photovoltaic modules has become increasingly crucial. Defect detection in photovoltaic panels is essential within the photovoltaic industry, as it directly influences the performance and reliability of these modules. Nonetheless, challenges such as image noise and the small size of defect targets in surface defect detection frequently result in information loss during feature fusion. Firstly, ADP-GFPN (Adaptive Detail Preservation Generalized Feature Pyramid Network) module is proposed based on GFPN (Generalized Feature Pyramid Network), which further improves feature fusion efficiency and performance. This module boosts the ability of the model to detect small-sized defects while preserving more critical detail information. Secondly, Exponential Moving Average Slide (EMAS) Loss is proposed. The loss not only emphasizes hard samples during training but also balances the influence of historical and current observational data, resulting in a smoother and more stable loss value. This enhancement strengthens the model's robustness and generalization capability. Experimental results indicate that MFPD-Net outperforms the baseline, with a 5.4% increase in Precision and a 2.2% improvement in mAP50.

articleTitle: Autonomic Mobility Management of Heterogeneous Ubiquitous Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: As mobile internet rapidly develops and service requirement diversify, the complexity of mobile and handover scenarios is continually increasing. The ubiquity of mobile entities and the continuous development of virtual connectivity, along with fully covered heterogeneous networks, have increased the frequency of both horizontal and vertical handovers. Traditional mobility management schemes mainly solve the problem of horizontal handover, but there are still challenges in achieving efficient vertical handover in heterogeneous ubiquitous networks. Therefore, we propose a heterogeneous ubiquitous network autonomic mobility management framework based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and design an Autonomic Mobility Management Scheme (AMMS). Firstly, to achieve efficient network selection and resource optimization, the Multi- Agent Double Deep Q-Network(MA-DDON) is adopted. Then, to further improve the accuracy of handover decision, a Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network is trained for user trajectory prediction, Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed demonstrates good robustness, significantly improving the efficiency of network handovers and enhancing service availability, thereby meeting the demand for high-quality connectivity in complex and dynamic network environments.

articleTitle: 3D Hand Mesh Reconstruction Based on A Monocular RGB Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: Estimating the full 3D hand shape and pose from a single RGB image is essential for virtual reality and human-computer interaction applications, but it remains a challenging task. While current hand reconstruction methods have achieved high accuracy, they often come with heavy computational costs, limiting their ability to perform real-time inference. To tackle this issue, we present a novel learning-based network architecture that consists of two key components: (1) a 3D hand joint position detection module that efficiently extracts joint positions from hand images, and (2) an inverse kinematics module that precisely predicts joint rotations in a single feed forward pass. Comprehensive evaluations across several datasets demonstrate that our method generates accurate and realistic 3D hand meshes while outperforming existing methods in 3D hand pose estimation.

articleTitle: Application Analysis and Development Recommendations for the Generative Adversarial Networks in Enhancing Automobile Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: The security of data generated by vehicles during operation is critically important, especially as the number of intelligent and connected vehicle users continues to rise, leading to the rapid increase of automobile communication data. In response, researchers have employed GAN s to address data security challenges within this domain, achieving significant outcomes. This paper primarily focuses on personal information identification, data desensitization, and secure transmission of data within the framework of automobile data security. The latest research on GAN s is reviewed and analyzed to assess the feasibility, strengths, and limitations for automotive data security, and the insights into future development recommendations are also provided in this domain.

articleTitle: Dimensionality Reduction Algorithm With Ordered Pair Of Normalized Real Numbers
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: Before classifying high-dimensional data, dimension-ality reduction algorithms are often used to process the data to achieve the purpose of reducing computational complexity and interference of redundant information, and improving the correct rate of classification. However, various dimensionality reduction algorithms have their advantages and disadvantages, and their performance varies greatly in different datasets, and it is difficult to choose the optimal dimensionality reduction algorithm. To address this problem, this paper introduces a new mathematical concept of ordered pair of normalized real numbers into the field of dimensionality reduction algorithm for the first time, and puts forward the new method of combining different dimensionality reduction algorithms through ordered pair of normalized real numbers, to realize the complementarity of different dimensionality reduction algorithms, improve the accuracy of subsequent classification. In addition, this paper also proposes the nearest neighbor classification algorithm of ordered pair of normalized real numbers, which realizes the classification of ordered normalized real number pairs. Through experiments on multiple real data sets and comparing a variety of improved k-nearest neighbor algorithms, it is verified that the proposed method has better performance.

Author Keywords: Ordered pair of normalized real numbers

articleTitle: Integrating AI into Biology Education: Classifying Edible and Poisonous Mushrooms Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly prevalent in various domains, its integration into education offers unique opportunities to enhance learning experiences. This paper explores the application of AI, specifically machine learning, in biology education through the classification of edible and poisonous mushrooms. Leveraging a dataset of gilled mushrooms from the Agaricus and Lepiota families, this study demonstrates how AI techniques can be used to classify species based on morphological features such as cap shape, gill attachment, and color. The use of AI not only improves students' understanding of species identification and biological classification but also introduces them to key concepts in data science, such as feature selection, model training, and validation. By implementing machine learning algorithms like decision trees and support vector machines, students can engage in interactive learning experiences that merge biology with modern technological tools. The results show that integrating AI into biology curricula can foster both scientific literacy and computational thinking, offering a more comprehensive and engaging approach to science education. This paper outlines a practical framework for educators to incorporate AI in biology lessons, preparing students for future academic and career challenges in an increasingly digital world.

articleTitle: Trajectory Prediction of High-Mobility Targets Based on Self-Attention Mechanism and Bilstm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: High maneuvering target trajectory has high complexity and uncertainty, and it is very easy to cause trajectory prediction accuracy to be difficult to satisfy due to model mismatch in the process of target tracking. To address this problem, a data-driven composite prediction method is proposed. Considering that the target high maneuvering trajectory is characterized by continuity, temporal sequence, and short duration, a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a bidirectional long and short time memory network (Bi-LSTM) are used to learn the spatial dimension features and temporal dimension features of the input data, respectively; the fusion of self-attention mechanism (AT) assigns weights to the outputs of the CNN-Bi-LSTM to dynamically adjust the degree of attention at different time steps according to the time series, thus focusing on the key information; using MAE as an indicator, the model hyperparameters are adjusted using the Dung Beetle Algorithm (DBO) to determine the optimal prediction model. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is illustrated by setting up comparative ablation experiments. The simulation results show that compared with the CNN model, the MAE of the proposed model is reduced by 44% on average, which can effectively improve the accuracy of high maneuvering trajectory prediction.

articleTitle: Research on Personalized Recommendation Algorithms Based on Collaborative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: Traditional recommendation algorithms often suffer from issues such as data sparsity, lack of memory association, and prediction accuracy. This paper proposes a collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm that integrates memory and balance factors. When analyzing user interests and preferences, there are optimal design from multiple aspects such as memory factors and novelty of objects. This paper introduces a memory weight function to reflect the temporal characteristics of user interests, and incorporates a balance factor into user similarity calculation to reduce the impact of popular items on user similarity calculation, thus improving the accuracy of user similarity calculation. Experimental validation is conducted on the MovieLens dataset using MAE as the evaluation metric. The results demonstrate significant improvements in the experimental metrics, indicating enhanced recommendation accuracy and improved resilience to data sparsity.

articleTitle: Accelerated Scaled Gradient Descent Algorithm For Low-Rank Matrix Factorization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computer Engineering and Intelligent Control (ICCEIC)
abstract: Low-rank matrix factorization is a particularly effective method which finds numerous applications in signal processing, machine learning and imaging science. Recent literature has proposed that scaled gradient descent (ScaledGD) algorithm. It achieves linear convergence without depending on the condition number, while maintaining the low per-iteration cost. The task of this paper is to propose an accelerated ScaledGD algorithmic approach called scaled momentum algorithm, which using a method similar to momentum to accelerate ScaledGD. Momentum is a commonly used optimization algorithm in deep learning that helps accelerate gradient descent in the relevant direction and dampens oscillations. The new scaled momentum algorithm has a benign convergence guarantee similar to the ScaledGD that is independent of the number of conditions, while prominently improve the rate of convergence than ScaledGD.
